title: President's Role in a Parliamentary Democracy

facts.t: Ireland's President can ask the Supreme Court whether a Bill is constitutional
facts.d: Article 26 of the Irish Constitution lets the head of state refer a Bill for pre-assent review. India's Article 143 reference belongs to the government, not the President's own judgement — a genuine check the Indian office lacks.

facts.t: Impeachment under Article 61 has never once been attempted
facts.d: The procedure is so onerous — charges framed by either House, investigated, then passed by two-thirds of the total membership of both — that no President has ever faced it. Accountability rests almost entirely on convention.

facts.t: India is one of three parliamentary democracies that still legislate by ordinance
facts.d: India, Pakistan and Bangladesh. All three inherited the power from the Government of India Act, 1935. Ordinance promulgation peaked at 196 in the 1990s and 133 in the 1970s — both periods of political instability.

bank.q: With reference to the President's legislative role, consider the following statements:
s: The President may grant, withhold or return a Bill under Article 111.
A Money Bill may be returned for reconsideration.
There is no constitutional timeline for granting assent.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. A Money Bill cannot be returned — and the absence of a deadline is what creates the pocket veto.

bank.q: An ordinance must be approved by Parliament within:
bank.e: Six weeks of Parliament reassembling, under Article 123.

bank.q: Match List I (episode) with List II (significance):
pairs: A. Zail Singh and the Postal Bill
1. Returned a Cabinet recommendation for President's Rule
B. K. R. Narayanan and Bihar
C. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam and the Office of Profit Bill
3. Disqualification of twenty MLAs on ECI advice
4. The limits of the suspensive veto
bank.e: Zail Singh's inaction, Narayanan's assertive use of the Article 74(1) proviso, Kalam's compulsion to sign once the Bill returned unchanged, and Kovind's quasi-judicial disqualification function.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a discretionary or reserve power of the President?
o: Appointing a Prime Minister in a hung Lok Sabha
Returning ministerial advice once for reconsideration
Dismissing a government that has demonstrably lost its majority but refuses to resign
Refusing assent to a Money Bill
bank.e: A Money Bill cannot be returned, and refusing assent to it is not treated as a reserve power — it would simply defeat the government's financial business.

bank.as: The President's one-time reconsideration of advice is a weak check.
bank.rs: After the 44th Amendment the President must act on the advice if it is returned unchanged.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — precisely what constrained President Kalam over the Office of Profit Bill in 2006.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about clemency powers:
s: Article 72 is broader than Article 161 because it extends to death sentences.
Clemency is exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
Judicial review of clemency is entirely barred.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Limited review is available for arbitrariness, mala fides and undue delay.

bank.q: Which country's President may refuse to sign laws that are clearly unconstitutional?
bank.e: Germany's Federal President exercises a legal-formal review before signing. Ireland's distinctive power is the Article 26 reference to the Supreme Court.

bank.q: All of the following are identified as problems with the office EXCEPT:
o: Ambiguity in the scope of reserve powers
Absence of a codified post-poll alliance protocol
Delay on bills and mercy petitions
bank.e: Article 61 has never been successfully invoked — the problem is that accountability is too weak, not too frequent.

bank.q: President's Rule under Article 356 has been invoked approximately:
bank.e: Around 130 times. S. R. Bommai curbed but did not eliminate the practice.

bank.q: With reference to the proposed way forward, consider the following:
s: Codifying timelines for assent, ordinances and mercy petitions.
Introducing an Ireland-style pre-assent constitutional reference power for the President.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are proposed. On ordinances, the recommendation is transparency and a cap on re-promulgation, not abolition.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
items: K. R. Narayanan returns the Bihar recommendation
Zail Singh and the Postal Bill
Kalam and the Office of Profit Bill
bank.e: Zail Singh and the Postal Bill (1986) → S. R. Bommai (1994) → Narayanan on Bihar (1998) → Kalam and the Office of Profit Bill (2006).

bank.as: The President's neutrality is often questioned.
bank.rs: The office is filled by an electoral college dominated by the ruling coalition, and holders frequently have a prior political career.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — hence the proposal to insulate the office from political career pipelines, on the model of the British Speaker's visible detachment.
